description: Link an Artifact to the Capability or Component it REALIZES — the file, drawing or binary that implements it, as opposed to one that merely describes it (`documents`). This is the as-built half of the design: a capability nothing realizes is raised as `unrealized_capability`, and `reconcile_artifacts` compares each realizing file's checksum against its recorded baseline to catch drift. `link_artifact` does this in one call with provenance and a checksum, and is the better door; use this when the Artifact node already exists. Ask for this when you want to record that a real file implements a capability or part.

artifact_id.description: The registered Artifact (`art:…`) that implements the target in code or hardware. For a document that describes rather than implements, use `documents`.

completeness.description: `stub` / `partial` / `complete` — how much of the thing EXISTS.

conformance.description:
`unchecked` (default) / `reviewed` / `verified` — whether anyone
confirmed the artifact still DOES WHAT THE TARGET REQUIRES. A different
question from `completeness`, and from the Artifact's `checksum`, which
says only that the file has not MOVED. Leave it off unless somebody
actually checked: `unchecked` is the honest reading, and the count of
unchecked links is the point (`evidence_report`).

target_id.description: The realized node; its type is `target_type`.

target_type.description:
Node type the artifact realizes (e.g. `Capability`, `Component`).
Optional since 2026-09-06: resolved from the id when omitted (the id
prefix names the type); an id held by more than one type is REFUSED, never
guessed — pass it then.

name: realizes
